g.text: n = 1: sd of means 114.8 km (σ/√n = 113.2), skewness 3.31 (γ/√n = 3.4), 95.0% within ±1.96
n = 5: sd of means 51.8 km (σ/√n = 50.6), skewness 1.32 (γ/√n = 1.52), 94.4% within ±1.96
n = 30: sd of means 20.1 km (σ/√n = 20.7), skewness 0.41 (γ/√n = 0.62), 96.6% within ±1.96
n = 100: sd of means 10.6 km (σ/√n = 11.3), skewness 0.24 (γ/√n = 0.34), 97.0% within ±1.96

svg.text: Notice: the means of 30 or 100 depths fall on the bell curve though single depths are nowhere near normal, and their spread shrinks as σ/√n (km in each header). Skewness fades
only as 1/√n, so n = 5 is still lopsided: 'n ≥ 30' is a rule of thumb, not a law. Caveat: draws are with replacement from one month's quakes, by a deterministic pseudo-random
generator, so the same data give the same samples.
